questions.prompt: How many legs does a spider have?
questions.factOneLiner: Insects have six, which is the easiest way to tell the two apart.

questions.prompt: What is the largest animal on Earth?
questions.factOneLiner: Its heart alone can weigh as much as a small car.

questions.prompt: Which planet is closest to the sun?
questions.factOneLiner: A year there lasts just eighty eight Earth days.

questions.prompt: Which gas makes up most of the air we breathe?
questions.factOneLiner: It is about seventy eight percent of the atmosphere, well ahead of oxygen.

questions.prompt: What is the fastest land animal?
questions.factOneLiner: It can only hold top speed for about half a minute before overheating.

questions.prompt: How many chambers does the human heart have?
questions.factOneLiner: Two atria on top collect blood, two ventricles below push it out.

questions.prompt: What do bees collect from flowers to make honey?
questions.factOneLiner: A single hive may visit two million flowers for one jar of it.

questions.prompt: What is the largest organ of the human body?
questions.factOneLiner: An adult carries roughly two square metres of it.

questions.prompt: Which vitamin does sunlight help your body produce?
questions.factOneLiner: Ten minutes of midday sun is often enough to make a day's worth.

questions.prompt: What is a group of lions called?
questions.factOneLiner: They are the only cats that live in permanent social groups.

questions.prompt: What is the centre of an atom called?
questions.factOneLiner: It holds nearly all the mass in a tiny fraction of the volume.

questions.prompt: Which sea creature can regrow a lost arm?
questions.factOneLiner: Some species can regrow an entire body from one severed arm.

questions.prompt: What is the process plants use to turn sunlight into food?
questions.factOneLiner: It is where almost all the oxygen in the atmosphere came from.

questions.prompt: Roughly how long does sunlight take to reach Earth?
questions.factOneLiner: So the sun you see has always already moved on.

questions.prompt: What is the study of earthquakes called?
questions.factOneLiner: The instruments that record them are sensitive enough to detect distant storms.

questions.prompt: Which planet has the most prominent ring system?
questions.factOneLiner: The rings are mostly water ice, and only about ten metres thick in places.

questions.prompt: What kind of animal is a Komodo dragon?
questions.factOneLiner: It is the largest lizard alive, reaching about three metres.

questions.prompt: Which part of the brain controls balance and coordination?
questions.factOneLiner: It holds more neurons than the rest of the brain combined.

questions.prompt: What is frozen carbon dioxide commonly called?
questions.factOneLiner: It skips the liquid stage entirely and turns straight into gas.

questions.prompt: Which blood cells fight infection?
questions.factOneLiner: They are outnumbered by red cells roughly seven hundred to one.
